issues.description: Element: interface for milking animals (method: String messageOnMilk()). Problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Milkable' with an abstract method messageOnMilk(). The solution repository instead defines an interface named 'Dairy' (package de.tum.cit.ase.Dairy) with the method String messageOnMilk(), and the Goat and Seal classes implement Dairy. The solution repository also contains a Milkable.java file that is empty. This naming mismatch (Milkable vs Dairy) plus the empty Milkable.java file creates confusion for students: they will implement or use Milkable as specified in the exercise, but the reference solution and some solution classes use Dairy, preventing a direct one-to-one comparison and leading to compilation or evaluation mismatches when comparing student submissions against the solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes (choose one):
1) Rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (file: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java), update its declaration to 'public interface Milkable { String messageOnMilk(); }', and update Goat and Seal to implement Milkable. Remove the empty Milkable.java file if present or replace it with the correct interface. OR
2) Update the problem statement and template to refer to 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable' (and update example usages in Main.java), and remove the empty Milkable.java from the solution repository. Ensure exactly one interface file exists with the single method signature: String messageOnMilk(); so students and the reference solution use the same identifier.

issues.description: Concept: the interface representing animals that can be milked. Problem statement / UML and the template code refer to this interface as 'Milkable' (interface name in the UML and usages in Main.java). In the solution repository the corresponding interface is declared as 'Dairy' (Dairy.java) and concrete classes (Seal.java, Goat.java) implement 'Dairy'. The solution also contains an empty Milkable.java file. This divergent identifier naming (Milkable vs Dairy) maps the same conceptual entity to different names across artifacts and will confuse students: they will implement or look for 'Milkable' as required by the exercise, but the solution code uses 'Dairy', and the empty Milkable.java in the solution further obscures intent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (Dairy.java -> Milkable.java), update Seal.java and Goat.java to implement Milkable, and remove or replace the empty Milkable.java file in the solution. Ensure the template, problem statement/UML, and solution all consistently use 'Milkable'. Alternatively (less preferred) update the problem statement/UML and template to use 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable' so all artifacts match.
